binding_detection.definition: Threshold-free detection of unresolved bindings from each run's own P(unresolved) over its binding items; the positive class is gold unresolved. auroc is the Mann-Whitney AUROC (a tied pair counts one half); average_precision is the step-wise area under the precision-recall curve (sklearn's definition). Both are league bootstraps over the same draws. flagged counts items predicted unresolved: the argmax of the two probabilities, or the run's decision when it has none. mcc is a copy of the leaderboard's binding MCC point. Runs without probabilities (the baselines and the gold_view ceiling) have null auroc and average_precision.

consistency.definition: Local-conflict rate of one run's raw answers, with no gold and no floor. Two predicates are reported separately. MAIN: a set of answers is contradictory when (a) its clauses and the facts are unsatisfiable, or (b) some outcome literal is forced false (it reaches its negation), or (c) a deferred cardinality part is violated, or (d) it contains an invalid group. Rule (b) is justified by the fixture's world: hard_suite.constants() excludes gold-constant outcomes from relations and groups, so no listed outcome is constant in the world the suite describes, and an answer set that forces an outcome constant contradicts that world. UNSAT-ONLY is the same predicate without (b): (a), (c) and (d). Outcome variables are the outcome ids. Each market has the outcomes :1 and :2, and the complement facts (x1 or x2) and (not x1 or not x2) hold for every market (market membership from gold/meta.jsonl, checked against gold/bindings.jsonl). The facts are never counted as answers. Markets are treated independently: paraphrase identities between markets (shared candidate classes) are not used, so a conflict that arises only through two markets that state the same proposition is not counted (an under-count). A relation answer (pred not NONE, MISSING or None, and not abstained) contributes the clauses of harness/fixed.py _relation_clauses. A group answer contributes the scorer's canonical class (decision_scoring: the lower bound is the largest exactly_one or at_least_k over the unscoped decisions on its members, the upper bound the smallest exactly_one, at_most_one or at_most_k, and the first ordered_chain), not every raw decision. Its terms (ordered_chain, exactly_one, at_most_one, at_least_k:K, at_most_k:K) are compiled by fixed._group_units (scope None, direction forward; an ordered_chain uses the row's chain, member i implies member i+1). An invalid group (lower bound above upper bound) is contradictory alone. Its non-2-CNF parts (at least k of m with 1 <= k < m and m > 2, including exactly_one's at-least-one for m > 2; at most k with 1 < k < m) are deferred cardinality checks with harness/admit.py at_least_possible and at_most_possible on the closure. These checks are sound but not complete: a violation is a real contradiction, a missed one is not counted. A minimal contradictory set (for either predicate) is a contradictory set of at most 3 answers none of whose proper subsets is contradictory under that predicate; a single answer that is contradictory alone is a minimal set of size 1. An answer is conflicting under a predicate when it belongs to at least one minimal set of that predicate; its size is the smallest such set under MAIN. The enumeration tests every connected set of at most 3 answers (connected through shared markets: a contradiction of a set with two market-disjoint parts lies in one part, so minimal sets are connected), with each set tested against its singles and its pairs. A pair that shares no market is not tested, because it is contradictory only if one of its answers is, and that answer is excluded already. No cycle test or literal-order heuristic is used. contradiction_detected is the MAIN predicate applied to all claim-bearing answers together (sound, not complete). NONE answers, none groups, abstained answers, MISSING or None preds (unanswered or errored, so no claim), readings and bindings are not claim-bearing and are not scored. Readings are not used: the group class already drops scoped decisions, and relations have no scope. Release analysis: an answer is conflicting if it belongs to a minimal conflict under either predicate (MAIN or UNSAT-only), so conflicting_unsat is part of conflicting in total and in every op. conflicting_main counts the answers in a minimal MAIN conflict (UNSAT, forced outcome, cardinality or invalid group). by_size is the smallest witness under the main predicate (UNSAT, forced outcome, cardinality or invalid group) for each conflicting_main answer, so sum(by_size) == conflicting_main; an answer only in a minimal UNSAT-only conflict has no main witness and is not in by_size.

cost.hardware: 2× NVIDIA RTX A6000 (48 GB), Ollama 0.40.11 (CUDA), one server per GPU, OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=2
cost.note: From the single published run per model; build-phase wall clock, includes harness overhead.

judged.sample_rule: PREREG.md: all 423 all_wrong items; 127 inverted (not all_wrong) items, stratified by op x gold class x stratum; 50 unflagged controls, stratified the same way over the unflagged items

method.b_comparison: the leaderboard's ci95 and the CI file are B = 2000 intervals (their draws are the first 2000 of this module's B = 20000); the rank intervals, pairwise intervals, p-values and depth intervals here are the B = 20000 paired draws
method.calibration: Brier is summed over the options (range 0 to 2); calibration is copied from each cell's score_decisions, not rescored
method.cost: decisions is the cell's decision count (one per decision item; a reading's base and alt rows count once); decisions_per_s is decisions over the leaderboard's build_wall_s
method.diff: diff = a minus b (point and draws); the README shows higher minus lower
method.family: per metric: headline, relation, group; each family is corrected separately, not against the others
method.headline: relation_group_mcc: the mean of the relation and group MCC over the same draws
method.higher: the model with the larger point estimate when resolved; null when not resolved
method.interval: 95% percentile interval (numpy, linear) of the valid draws
method.item_audit: per op the halves are the models ranked by the op's own MCC; all_wrong is over the 15 models; inverted is computed on residuals within (op, gold class, stratum) cells; see item_audit.null_inverted_rate

null_inverted_rate.population: all item_audit items; shares of inverted items under random 7-vs-7 splits

method.p_value: per pair, delta = a - b per draw: p = min(1, 2 * (1 + min(#delta<=0, #delta>=0)) / (1 + B_valid))
method.rank: rank is the point rank among the 15 models; ci95 is the 2.5% (method lower) to 97.5% (method higher) range of the per-draw rank; median by method nearest
method.repeats: the published run r1 is the reference and is not listed; identical, delta_vs_published and flip_rate are computed over the 10,716 prediction rows and the published headline
method.runs: the 15 models in headline rank order, then the baselines with decisions (heuristic, lexical, embedding, gold_view, hf)
method.uncertainty: league resampling of the one fixture is the only uncertainty source; one deterministic run per model

repeats.note_protocol: Diagnostic only: the leaderboard headline remains the single pre-registered run; repeats use the pre-registered command on CUDA (Ollama 0.40.11, both A6000s).
repeats.note_shuffle: shuffle = one pass with answer options presented in a seeded random order (MB_S1_OPTION_SEED=20261101); same model, weights and prompts otherwise.
repeats.note_vulkan: vulkan = the d3:9b repeats run on Ollama's Vulkan backend instead of CUDA (two passes, r2 and r3, which must agree); reported as a backend-sensitivity diagnostic.
